messages:
Alex: Heads-up — saw a tail-latency regression on prod after yesterday's kernel-picker change. p95 went from ~120ms -> ~260ms for seq_len=2048 workloads. KV cache hit-rate dropped ~8%.
Mira: Saw that in the traces too. Replayed a few requests. Looks like microbatch gating is causing a handoff into the small-batch warp-specialist path which then picks a kernel with high reg usage -> spills.
Sam: Can you paste the profiler output/snippet? Which device was this on?
Alex: Repro profile (trimmed):
```
Device: A100-80GB
workload: chat-infer
seq=2048
microbatch=4
kernel_chosen: tilerouter_v3_warp_spec
est_regs: 68 -> actual spills
smem_alloc: 56KB
p95: 260ms
kv_hit_before: 0.92
kv_hit_after: 0.84
```
Mira: Ok this explains it. tilerouter_v3 picks tile_size=64 to boost occupancy for short sequences, but for long sequences register pressure increases due to unrolled loops -> spill. The microbatch handoff threshold made many long requests land on that path.
Jorge: FWIW tile_size=48 usually reduces reg usage without huge occupancy loss on A100s. Also prefetch distance changes the live-range of registers — prefetch=8 vs 16 made a ~6% p95 diff in my microbench.
Sam: Our microbatcher config today: `max_microbatch=8, gating_threshold=0.6, seq_len_heuristic=autocalc`. Maybe the gating logic is too coarse and batches based on queue depth rather than sequence-length distribution. We should weight seq_len when choosing the handoff target.
Mira: Two quick mitigations: (1) add a reg_estimate guard in kernel_picker: if est_regs > 60 then avoid warp_spec kernel for seq>1024; (2) lower microbatch gating aggressiveness for long-seq workloads.
Alex: Agreed. Also want to avoid KV cache thrash — when handoffs flip kernels we get different KV layout and more evictions. We should measure KV reuse per kernel path.
Jorge: I ran a small experiment: forcing tile_size 48 for warp_spec on A100 reduces est_regs to ~54 and p95 moves back to ~140ms. KV hit-rate recovered.
Sam: Can we add a lightweight regression test in CI that runs a seq_len sweep [128, 512, 1024, 2048] with KV cache enabled and microbatcher on? If p95 for any seq>1024 increases >20% vs baseline, fail. I can add it.
Tia: Who pushed the kernel-picker change? We need a rollback plan and a controlled canary while we patch.
Mira: That was my rollout last night — I was tuning small-batch latency. I scoped the change too broadly, missed the seq>1024 path. Sorry.
InfraBot: deploy-redwood-runtime v2.7.1 -> prod (id: db3a) by Mira at 2026-03-15T02:11:22Z :white_check_mark:
Alex: No worries, thanks for owning it. Proposal for steps: (A) revert the rollout on prod canary, (B) add reg_estimate guard + tile_size fallback, (C) add CI seq_len sweep, (D) canary deploy patched picker. Assign owners?
Mira: I'll revert rollout on the canary now.
Jorge: I'll prepare a small patch to cap tile_size for warp_spec and add `if est_regs > 60 -> fallback_kernel=tilerouter_v2_prefetch` in the picker.
Sam: I'll add the CI test and a perf baseline job for the next release.
Tia: I'll own the canary checklist and monitoring. Need a dashboard alert for KV hit-rate and p95 tail for long seqs.
Alex: I'll create the alerts: alert if p95>200ms for seq>1024 OR kv_hit_drop > 5% over 5min.
Mira: Reverting now.
InfraBot: deploy-redwood-runtime v2.7.0 -> prod (rollback) by Mira at 2026-03-15T02:20:40Z :rocket:
Sam: Great. After rollback let's keep microbatcher conservative (lower gating_threshold) until selector gets seqlen-aware.
Jorge: Also let's add a tiny microbench in the kernel autotuner that reports est_regs vs actual spill_count for each tile_size — will help catch reg-pressure regressions early.
Alex: Good call. Follow-ups: Mira->revert, Jorge->picker patch + autotuner metric, Sam->CI sweep, Tia->canary + alerts, Alex->watch metrics. I'll file a short RFC in the repo with the autotune changes.
Mira: Thanks all. I'll update this thread when rollback is live and canary metrics look good.
Alex: LGTM. Moving the rest of the discussion to #eng-runtime-ops for action tracking. :thumbsup:
